plan.planning_summary: The problem requests a design optimization for a specific two-layer antireflection coating with fixed materials (SiO2, TiO2) and strict thickness bounds (40-160 nm). Since no literature was retrieved, the strategy relies entirely on theoretical optimization of the geometric degrees of freedom. The single distinct axis available is the simultaneous tuning of layer order and individual layer thicknesses to minimize broadband reflectance. Because the maximum number of routes is 1, and the problem has only one viable geometric configuration space (two layers, two materials), a single route encompassing both possible stack orders as discrete choices within the search space is the correct approach. This route will vary the thickness of both layers and select the optimal ordering, treating the order as a categorical design variable or by evaluating both topologies if the solver supports it, but strictly adhering to the constraint of exactly one SiO2 and one TiO2 layer.

routes.title: Optimization of Two-Layer SiO2/TiO2 Antireflection Coating Geometry
routes.scientific_hypothesis: There exists a combination of layer order (SiO2-first or TiO2-first) and layer thicknesses within the 40-160 nm range that minimizes the arithmetic mean power reflectance below the soft target of 0.03 across the 450-700 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Destructive interference of reflected waves at the air-coating and coating-substrate interfaces. The optimal thicknesses depend on the refractive index contrast and the specific sequence of high/low index layers relative to the incident medium and substrate.
routes.proposed_topology: Air (n=1.0) / Layer 1 (Variable Material: sio2 or tio2, Variable Thickness) / Layer 2 (Variable Material: tio2 or sio2, Variable Thickness) / Glass Substrate (n=1.52). Exactly two layers total.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm, 5 nm step, s-pol, normal incidence)
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thickness must be strictly between 40 nm and 160 nm
Exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2 required
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for multilayer optics
Thin film interference conditions for broadband antireflection
expected_advantages: Directly addresses the user's specific material and thickness constraints
Explores the full feasible design space for the two-layer system
known_risks: The global minimum may lie outside the 40-160 nm thickness bounds
The fixed refractive indices may not allow a mean reflectance below 0.03 with only two layers
routes.execution_request_english: Perform a deterministic optimization using the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for a planar two-layer stack on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52, lossless) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must contain exactly one layer of 'SiO2 (Gao)' (n=1.46, lossless) and one layer of 'TiO2 (Siefke)' (n=2.40, lossless). Evaluate both possible layer orders: (1) Air/SiO2 (Gao)/TiO2 (Siefke)/Glass and (2) Air/TiO2 (Siefke)/SiO2 (Gao)/Glass. For each order, optimize the thickness of both layers, constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm inclusive. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees) over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled every 5 nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations per round. Report the best candidate's layer order, thicknesses, full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not claim the target (<0.03) is met without verifying the computed mean against the reported spectrum.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If the optimization yields a mean reflectance significantly above 0.03 and the thicknesses are pinned against the 40 nm or 160 nm bounds, conclude that the two-layer constraint with these specific materials cannot meet the target within the given manufacturing limits.
